"statement": "Let $k$ be a positive integer, and let $G$ be a complete geometric graph on $2k$ points. A **$k$-staircase** is the point-set construction defined earlier in the source. **Staircase characterization conjecture.** If $G$ admits a decomposition into $k+1$ plane star-forests and the convex hull of $V(G)$ has size $k+1$, then $V(G)$ can be described as a $k$-staircase.\nThe source reports that computations on point sets with $6$ and $8$ points found no counterexamples, but gives no proof or resolution. "statement": "Let $n\ge3$ be odd, and let $G$ be a complete geometric graph on $n$ vertices that can be decomposed into $\left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil+1$ plane star-forests. **Convex-hull-size conjecture.** The convex hull of the vertex set $V(G)$ has size at most

$$
\left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil+1.
$$

For even order, the source proves the analogous bound when $n=2k$, while the odd-order case is proposed as a conjecture. Its general validity remains open.",

"title": "Pach–Saghafian–Schnider conjecture on decompositions of cliques into k-star-forests",

"statement": "A **$k$-star-forest** is a star-forest with at most $k$ connected components. Let $F_k(n)$ be the minimum integer such that the complete graph on $n$ vertices can be decomposed into $F_k(n)$ $k$-star-forests.

**Pach–Saghafian–Schnider conjecture.** For any $n\ge k\ge 2$,

$$
F_k(n)\ge \left\lceil\frac{(k+1)n}{2k}\right\rceil.
$$

This lower bound asserts that the construction obtained from the broken double-star decomposition together with matchings of size at most $k$ is best possible for decomposing cliques into $k$-star-forests. The statement is presented as a conjecture in the source; no resolution is given here.",
